findingDetails.title: Manifest paths can redirect sync writes outside package roots
findingDetails.case: A user runs vendor-sync pull or push with a manifest whose local_path, upstream_path, or include entry escapes its package root.
findingDetails.claim: Manifest-derived paths are joined to repository roots without rejecting absolute or parent-traversal paths, and copy/delete operations later use those paths.
findingDetails.evidence: resolve_dirs joins local_path and upstream_path directly; copy_tree deletes an existing target for a full pull and writes included files directly. A manifest-only change can plant the trigger, but a trusted operator must still invoke a mutating command.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the trigger requires changing the script and whether an automatic privileged caller was established. A data-only manifest change is sufficient after the manifest is tracked; no automatic pull/push caller was established. In this checkout git status reports vendor.json and both sync/build scripts as untracked phase additions, contrary to the prompt's tracked-file premise.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The manifest is normally maintained with the repository and pull/push are explicit operator actions, so this is a guarded local-tool path error rather than an unattended remote exploit.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if mutating sync commands are only run on reviewed manifests and no untrusted manifest reaches them; upgrade if privileged CI runs pull/push on untrusted changes.
findingDetails.userImpact: A malformed or adversarial manifest can overwrite or remove data outside the intended package directories when a mutating sync command runs.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Static path review covers resolve_dirs plus both pull and push paths into copy_tree; no path containment check precedes the writes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject absolute paths and traversal, resolve local/upstream paths beneath their roots, and validate every include path before any read or write.

findingDetails.title: Plugin build can delete an external skills directory through a symlinked parent
findingDetails.case: A build runs with claude-plugin resolving through a symlinked parent whose external target already contains .claude-plugin/plugin.json and a skills directory.
findingDetails.claim: shutil.rmtree follows a symlinked parent while removing the skills path, but the trigger requires the parent to resolve to an existing external plugin tree with a readable manifest.
findingDetails.evidence: build reads plugin.json before computing and removing skills. A symlink at the skills leaf is handled by rmtree's refusal path; the reported case requires a symlink higher in the path and a target satisfying the earlier manifest read.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether an ordinary tracked-file change can create the required external target and whether the manifest read blocks an absent target. The pre-rmtree read requires a valid plugin.json at the resolved parent; no build workflow that supplies such an external target was established. Current plugin files are untracked additions in this checkout.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: This is primarily a local workspace footgun if a developer deliberately points the plugin directory at another existing plugin tree; a party able to create that filesystem layout can also write broadly in the build workspace.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Close if the build is restricted to a fresh checkout with a real claude-plugin directory and no externally prepared parent symlink; upgrade if untrusted PR content can make a privileged runner resolve the parent to an existing external plugin tree.
findingDetails.userImpact: If the filesystem precondition is met, the build can remove the target tree's skills directory.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The reviewed sequence is manifest read at line 110, then skills removal at line 119; no normal in-repository data field selects an outside output directory.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve and validate the plugin/output paths against the repository root before cleanup, and refuse symlinked parents.

findingDetails.title: Plugin build can package content from a symlinked hub source
findingDetails.case: A shipped root hub file is replaced by a symlink to a path readable by the process running the plugin build.
findingDetails.claim: The symlink scan runs for packet trees, while HUB_FILES are inserted into the source map without a symlink check; copyfile and hashing follow a hub-source symlink.
findingDetails.evidence: A contributor can submit a symlinked hub source without changing the builder, but the impact depends on an external sensitive target and a privileged build context. No privileged untrusted-PR build or secret-bearing target was established.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether all shipped source trees share the same symlink scan and whether the copy/hash comparison detects a followed source link. Packet trees are scanned; HUB_FILES are not. The copy/hash comparison reads resolved bytes and does not detect the link itself.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Most ordinary in-repository symlink targets are public files, and the builder may run only on trusted local content. Secret packaging requires a sensitive target and execution/publishing path not established here.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Close if the build rejects or proves containment of every HUB_FILES source before reading; upgrade if privileged automated builds consume untrusted symlink changes and publish output.
findingDetails.userImpact: A privileged build could include readable external content in the generated plugin package.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The scan loop at lines 74-83 covers packet directories only; HUB_FILES are mapped at lines 71-72 then copied at lines 121-125.
findingDetails.recommendation: Apply symlink and resolved-root checks to every HUB_FILES source before copying or hashing.

findingDetails.title: Hosted rollback can clear unrelated content on the target page
findingDetails.case: A hosted diagram write is incomplete or wrong and the operator follows the documented rollback on a page that already contains unrelated objects.
findingDetails.claim: The rollback instruction clears the whole FigJam page and relies on the unverified claim that nothing else imports that page.
findingDetails.evidence: The hosted route names the plan but does not require an empty or dedicated page before writes. Its rollback clears the entire page; the general gate requires disclosure and approval but does not establish the page's contents.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked for a dedicated-page or empty-page precondition and item-scoped hosted rollback. Neither appears in the reviewed route.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: If users always choose a newly created empty page, clearing that page removes only the failed diagram; the current instructions do not enforce that condition.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the hosted route requires and verifies a dedicated empty page or uses item-scoped deletion for rollback.
findingDetails.userImpact: Following the documented rollback can delete unrelated FigJam content.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The hosted rollback is whole-page; the fallback route separately uses page duplication and version history.
findingDetails.recommendation: Require a verified dedicated empty page before the first hosted write, or make rollback remove only the generated diagram.

findingDetails.title: Flow delivery reply conflicts with the global self-scan rule
findingDetails.case: A Flow Mode response follows the two-line-only delivery instruction while active global Product Owner instructions require an HVR self-scan in every delivery response.
findingDetails.claim: The Flow reply says it carries the board and proof, and nothing else; the root instructions require a separate self-scan line as delivery metadata and do not exempt Flow Mode from it.
findingDetails.evidence: The Flow section requires board URL and read-back lines and says nothing else. AGENTS.md requires the HVR self-scan beside delivery verification and says the metadata belongs in chat.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the Flow exemption explicitly waives the self-scan. It waives export/file steps and defines board/read-back output, but the global rule still says every delivery response and its exemption text does not mention the scan.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The two-line Flow reply might be read as the specialized delivery shape overriding generic response metadata, making the global scan instruction ambiguous rather than impossible.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the global instructions explicitly exempt Flow Mode from the self-scan, or the Flow reply shape is amended to allow the metadata line.
findingDetails.userImpact: The agent cannot satisfy both mandatory response contracts for a Flow delivery.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The conflict is present in the root instruction surface and routed Flow Mode response section; it is not a one-off response.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reconcile the Flow reply shape with the global scan metadata rule.

findingDetails.title: Clarification requests can be routed to the Figma tool packet
findingDetails.case: A request names a figma-ds-cli operation and asks for a clarification without using a listed artifact word or dollar command, such as asking to draft a clarification about Flow output.
findingDetails.claim: The hub contract says clarification requests use the Product Owner packet, but artifactWords omits clarification; route_stage_one therefore returns the Figma packet when the tool signal is present.
findingDetails.evidence: The artifact check consults only routerPolicy.artifactWords before collecting tool-signal hits. With no listed artifact word or command, the figma-ds-cli signal is the only hit and routes to mcp-figma. check_hub.py checks only that artifactWords is a non-empty list and its fixed gold rows do not cover clarification.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked the hub's explicit clarification statement, configured artifactWords, routing precedence, and gold-row coverage. Clarification is named in the packet table but absent from words and examples that force the default.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The author may expect clarification requests to include task/doc/Story vocabulary or a command; the hub promises clarification requests directly, and the packet accepts clarification as an outcome.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only if the hub contract is narrowed so clarification is not independently a Product Owner request; otherwise add the term and a gold row.
findingDetails.userImpact: A clarification request can start in the tool-only packet, bypassing Product Owner intake and delivery behavior.
findingDetails.scopeProof: route_stage_one checks the configured list and returns the sole matching signal; the checker has no parity assertion between the list and documented packet coverage.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add clarification to the artifact vocabulary and a gate row, and make check_hub compare the documented policy inventory with hub-router.json.

findingDetails.title: Flow color limit has no check before or after the board write
findingDetails.case: A Mermaid model uses several classDef or style directives to assign different accent colors to categories.
findingDetails.claim: The extractor drops classDef/style directives before flow_check sees the diagram, and the documented read-back checks counts, labels and connector overlap without checking the one-accent limit.
findingDetails.evidence: Flow Mode limits the diagram to one accent. The parser discards style directives and flow_check only validates diagram kind, direction, shapes, labels, exits and node count. The read-back checklist does not mention accent count; live generator styling behavior was not tested.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked static pre-write validation and the written read-back instructions. The parser drops the directives and the read-back list checks counts, labels and connector geometry; no color-count check is stated.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The hosted generator may ignore Mermaid styling directives, or a human may inspect color as part of screenshot read-back. Neither behavior is established by the reviewed contract.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Close if the generator is shown to discard all styles or read-back explicitly verifies the one-accent rule; raise if the generator applies multiple colors and the checker is the sole gate.
findingDetails.userImpact: A generated board may violate the documented visual constraint and use color as a category scheme.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The parser counts and drops style directives and returns without preserving style properties; diagram_problems has no color/style condition.
findingDetails.recommendation: Reject or inspect style directives before writing, or state an explicit color check in board read-back.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A manifest path can escape package roots and redirect a mutating sync.

searchActions.result: Path joins are uncontained; destructive copy/delete is reachable only through explicit pull/push.

searchLedger.rationale: The path escape remains actionable, but the explicit mutating command lowers severity from P0 to P1.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A symlinked output parent can redirect recursive cleanup outside the repository.

searchActions.queryOrPath: build manifest read through skills rmtree
searchActions.result: The builder reads plugin.json before cleanup; the external parent must already expose a valid manifest and skills directory.

searchLedger.rationale: The local destructive condition is possible but an untrusted external trigger was not established; downgrade to P2.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A root hub symlink can make the plugin builder package bytes from outside the intended source.

searchActions.queryOrPath: HUB_FILES map, packet symlink scan, copy and hash
searchActions.result: The symlink scan is inside packet traversal only; root hub sources are copied and hashed by following their path.

searchLedger.rationale: A symlink change need not alter the builder, but privileged untrusted build and sensitive target were not established; downgrade to P2.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The hosted rollback can erase unrelated content on a non-empty page.

searchActions.queryOrPath: hosted write gate and rollback wording
searchActions.result: The gate names plan/page/effect; rollback still clears the whole page and no empty-page precondition is stated.

searchLedger.rationale: User approval of the write does not make whole-page rollback safe when page contents are unchecked.

searchLedger.invariant: Flow delivery and global delivery metadata instructions must be jointly satisfiable.

searchActions.queryOrPath: global Flow exemption, universal HVR line, and Flow reply shape
searchActions.result: Flow reply permits only board/proof while the global contract requires a separate self-scan metadata line.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A Product Owner artifact omitted from artifactWords can lose precedence to a tool signal.

searchActions.queryOrPath: clarification contract versus artifactWords and route_stage_one
searchActions.result: Clarification is promised in the Product Owner packet row but absent from artifactWords; a tool signal then wins. The gate only requires non-empty arrays and its gold rows omit clarification.

searchLedger.rationale: Current route behavior contradicts the explicit hub contract.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Style directives may carry more colors than the one-accent Flow rule allows.

searchActions.queryOrPath: style discard, diagram checks, and read-back checklist
searchActions.result: classDef/style statements are dropped before validation and neither checker nor read-back names an accent-count check.

searchLedger.rationale: The visual limit has no explicit validation step.

searchLedger.invariant: A tool signal preceded by a listed negation in its clause falls back to the default packet.

searchActions.queryOrPath: negation config, clause splitting, and gold rows
searchActions.result: The route applies a listed negation earlier in the same punctuation-split clause; gate rows cover long-distance, curly-apostrophe and prior-clause forms. The extra dont spelling is conservative but undocumented.

searchLedger.rationale: No unsafe current negation result was established; the extra alias routes conservatively to the default.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: Current behavior follows the stated within-clause rule for reviewed forms; vocabulary parity is included in the artifactWords gate recommendation.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Parser edge syntax may bypass shape, exit, node, or direction checks.

searchActions.queryOrPath: subgraphs, comments, ampersand endpoints, quotes, self-loops and decision exits
searchActions.result: Comments are removed; subgraphs add rejected container shapes; ampersand groups expand to emitted edges; outgoing edges count against each source decision; self-loops remain edges. Embedded | in quoted edge labels is outside the documented grammar and fails closed.

searchLedger.rationale: No acceptance bypass was found in the requested parser edges; style omission is tracked separately.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: The inspected edges map to explicit graph edges or fail closed under the documented Flow grammar.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Plugin manifests may contain inconsistent identity/version or unexpected server configuration.

searchActions.queryOrPath: both manifest objects and build refusal checks
searchActions.result: Names and versions agree, marketplace source is ./, plugin.json has no mcpServers, and builder refuses bin/.

searchLedger.rationale: No current manifest mismatch or unexpected server registration was found.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: Reviewed manifest fields are consistent and builder checks align with skills-only shape.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The model may violate the Flow checker contract or omit per-node provenance.

searchActions.queryOrPath: Mermaid block, declared counts and provenance rows
searchActions.result: Eight nodes have eight provenance rows; Mermaid has eight connectors and a two-exit labelled decision, matching the model count. Screenshot bytes were not in scope.

searchLedger.rationale: Internal counts, allowed node shapes, labels and provenance rows agree.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: Static comparison of model and its own provenance table found no inconsistency.
